A bill for an act relating to consumer protection; requiring certain energy generating facilities to be certified as child labor free; requiring certain products sold to be certified as child labor free; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapters 216I; 325D.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[+[216I.115] PROHIBITION ON CHILD LABOR FOR CERTAIN FACILITIES. +]

[+(a) The commission is prohibited from issuing a permit for a solar energy generating system or a wind energy conversion system under this chapter unless the applicant has demonstrated to the commission's satisfaction that no child labor, as defined under section 325D.75, subdivision 1, is used to manufacture the equipment used to construct and operate the solar energy generating system or wind energy conversion system. +]

[+(b) Paragraph (a) also applies to a solar energy generating system or a wind energy conversion system subject to local review under section 216I.08. +]

Sec. 2.

[+[325D.75] CHILD LABOR FREE PRODUCTS. +]

[+Subdivision 1.+]

[+Definitions.+]

[+(a) For purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given. +]

[+(b) "Child labor" has the meaning given in the International Labor Organization's Minimum Age Convention No. 138. +]

[+(c) "Solar photovoltaic device" has the meaning given in section 116C.7791. +]

[+(d) "Wind energy conversion system" has the meaning given in section 216I.02, subdivision 20. +]

[+Subd. 2.+]

[+Prohibition.+]

[+It is an unlawful trade practice to offer for sale in Minnesota any electric vehicle battery, solar photovoltaic device, or wind energy conversion system unless the electric vehicle battery, solar photovoltaic device, or wind energy conversion system's manufacturer certifies that no child labor was used to manufacture the electric vehicle battery, solar photovoltaic device, or wind energy conversion system. +]

[+Subd. 3.+]

[+Remedies.+]

[+A person that violates subdivision 2 is subject to the penalties established under section 325D.56. +]
bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to consumer protection; requiring certain energy generating facilities to be certified as child labor free; requiring certain products sold to be certified as child labor free; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapters 216I; 325D.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[216I.115] PROHIBITION ON CHILD LABOR FOR CERTAIN FACILITIES.

(a) The commission is prohibited from issuing a permit for a solar energy generating system or a wind energy conversion system under this chapter unless the applicant has demonstrated to the commission's satisfaction that no child labor, as defined under section 325D.75, subdivision 1, is used to manufacture the equipment used to construct and operate the solar energy generating system or wind energy conversion system.

(b) Paragraph (a) also applies to a solar energy generating system or a wind energy conversion system subject to local review under section 216I.08.

Sec. 2.

[325D.75] CHILD LABOR FREE PRODUCTS.

Subdivision 1.

Definitions.

(a) For purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given.

(b) "Child labor" has the meaning given in the International Labor Organization's Minimum Age Convention No. 138.

(c) "Solar photovoltaic device" has the meaning given in section 116C.7791.

(d) "Wind energy conversion system" has the meaning given in section 216I.02, subdivision 20.

Subd. 2.

Prohibition.

It is an unlawful trade practice to offer for sale in Minnesota any electric vehicle battery, solar photovoltaic device, or wind energy conversion system unless the electric vehicle battery, solar photovoltaic device, or wind energy conversion system's manufacturer certifies that no child labor was used to manufacture the electric vehicle battery, solar photovoltaic device, or wind energy conversion system.

Subd. 3.

Remedies.

A person that violates subdivision 2 is subject to the penalties established under section 325D.56.
